_sources.contours: DNAF-1: An Analytical Fallout Prediction Model and Code, DNA 6299F (1981), DTIC ADA130291, Table 3 (observed and predicted fallout pattern statistics) and Table 2 (test shot data).  Areas in km^2 inside each H+1 hour exposure-rate contour (R/hr), hotline length (km: the furthest distance from ground zero on the contour) and azimuth (degrees clockwise from north to that furthest point), as observed and as predicted by DNAF-1, DELFIC and WSEG-10.
_sources.shots: Compilation of Local Fallout Data from Test Detonations 1945-1962 Extracted from DASA 1251, Volume I (DNA 1251-1-EX, 1979), DTIC ADA079309: shot data pages and wind tables (Buster-Jangle Sugar: Table 12, H-hour; Sunbeam Small Boy: Table 109, H+5 minutes; Sunbeam Johnie Boy: Table 108, H-hour).

_notes: These are the bursts nearest the ground with well-measured close-in fallout: Sugar was a surface burst 3.5 ft up, Small Boy on a 10 ft tower, Johnie Boy 23 inches underground.  All three are within the fireball-on-the-ground case the map models.
Altitudes are feet above mean sea level, speeds statute miles per hour, directions the wind blows FROM.  Rows the tables leave blank are left out.

Fission yields: Sugar and Johnie Boy as DNAF-1 Table 2 gives them (all fission).  Small Boy's yield is classified in both sources ('low'); 1.65 kt is its later declassified yield, and it is taken to be all fission, as the other two are.
Small Boy's longitude is printed as 115 deg 55' 89.2", which cannot be; it is read as 115 deg 56' 29.2" (Frenchman Flat).
DNAF-1 gives no WSEG-10 prediction for Small Boy.
